newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields down,look to friendly budget.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields down,look to friendly budget.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed sharply lower as long end started to price in a market-friendly budget on May 13, offsetting the prospect of a rebound in this week's jobs data.
*Reserve Bank holds monthly board meeting on Tuesday.
Australian bond yields closed sharply lower as the long end started to price in a market-friendly budget on May 13, offsetting the prospect of a rebound in this week's jobs data.

The benchmark 10-year bond yield ended at its lowest level since end-February, taking a 16.7 percent leap in ANZ's April job advertisement series in its stride, and absorbing selling by institutional investors, traders said.
"I'm surprised we stood up so well considering the job ads. The market is obviously starting to expect a bond-friendly budget," one trader added.

Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Australia, said while the 1997/98 budget may not have the impact of last years, it is likely to be bond-friendly. "There may be some pleasant surprises and the government may meet its fiscal target sooner than previously thought," she said.
The government has said it aims to balance the budget by the 1998/99 fiscal year.

Meanwhile, the rise in job ads was the largest since the series began in 1975, although it partly reflected the earlier timing of Easter this year. However, ANZ analysts said even without this there would have been sizeable 5.0 percent growth.

Economists had already been predicting a rebound in employment of around 35,000 when the April labour force report is released on Thursday, although this is not expected to make much impression on the unemployment rate, which is seen staying at a high 8.7 percent.

Unemployment is expected to be high on the agenda when the Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting on Tuesday, although given last week's stronger than expected average weekly earnings, analysts expect policy to remain on hold.
RBA governor Ian Macfarlane is also due to face a parliamentary finance committee on Thursday.

The local market generally outperformed the dollar bloc, clawing back a large part of last week's spread widening following the wages data. The narrowing to the U.S. came despite another firm performance by U.S. Treasuries following a balanced budget accord on Friday. There was no Treasury trading in Japan.
The 10-year bond contract tested April's 92.250 high, and where a break could see the market make a further strong advance after finally overcoming major resistance at 92.210/92.230, traders added.
